feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iteration 3 (outer weights ±1.5, inner ±0.75, kp 5.0, kd 0.8, geometry at y=0.08 with ±0.06 m spread) scored 340.07, with oval finish rate 0.95 and s-bend exits at max_error 0.0609 with only 0.05 line losses per run. Iteration 4 showed that raising ki to 0.3 did not reduce the s-bend drift (still 0.0609, 0.10 losses) and lowered the oval finish rate to 0.85 (score 319.08). So the s-bend limit is not a steady bias that the integral can remove; it is turn rate per unit of steering command. Your wheel_track 0.10 change addresses that, and the Integrator has adopted it with the controller reverted to ki 0.1. Next race decision rules: if the s-bend still exits at about 0.061 m with line losses near zero, the track change is not enough and the next step is the slalom coverage change below. If the oval finish rate falls below 0.85 with steering_oscillation rising above about 0.3, the extra yaw is overshooting and wheel_track should go back toward 0.11.
requested_changes: If the s-bend still goes off track at max_error about 0.061 m with line_loss_events near 0 after wheel_track 0.10, keep wheel_track at 0.10 and move on to the slalom test. Iteration 3 (0.0609 with 0.05 losses) and iteration 4 (ki 0.3 gave the same 0.0609) show that controller integral gain does not cure this drift.

If the slalom still loses the line about once per run with the outer sensors reading near zero (iteration 3: 1.0 losses, progress 0.10), change sensor_size from 0.012 to 0.016 with the same x spread of ±0.06 and y of 0.08. A larger footprint keeps more tape in view at the edge, and the slalom has lost the line once per run in iterations 3 and 4.

If the oval finish rate falls below 0.85 with steering_oscillation above about 0.3 after the track change, change wheel_track from 0.10 to 0.11 m. Iteration 4 showed that more controller authority (ki 0.3) reduced the oval finish rate from 0.95 to 0.85, so the extra yaw from a narrower track may overshoot in the same way.
